article.title: Fight Facing the New Congress
article.author: Roxanne D. Brown
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. We sent a clear message on Election Day about what we want from the next Congress—affordability, accountability, and an economy that works for all. We’re disgusted with empty promises from a government that lavishes ever more on the do-nothing rich while working families fall further into the margins. We’ve had it with CEOs pocketing obscene sums while doling out scraps to everyone else and with billionaires frittering away huge sums to divide us. But tens of millions of working people just took back the wheel. We demonstrated how powerful we are when we come together. We showed that the future belongs to us , not to the 1 percent. And make no mistake, the path forward means making it easier for workers to form unions so we can continue to grow collective power and keep the uber-rich from siphoning away every good thing. Americans feel more disillusioned about the economy at present than they did during the depths of the pandemic. We’ve lost confidence in the nation’s institutions and see the country turning into something we no longer recognize. Related: Trump’s Canada Tariffs Put American Steel Jobs at Risk Yet growing numbers support unions like the United Steelworkers (USW) and want us to wield greater influence in American life. That’s because we’re committed, the way nobody else is, to building that economy for all. We force corporations to fork over a fair share, treat everyone equitably, and afford each person a voice. There’s no end to the affordability crisis—no strong middle class nor vibrant democracy, either—without more union workers. By banding together, workers win fair wages, affordable healthcare, safe working conditions, retirement security, and a seat at the table. Union workers, on average, make significantly higher wages and better benefits than nonunion peers. In turn, good union contracts enable us to double down on our communities. We support civic groups, volunteer our time, support local businesses, and advocate for good government, as we did leading up to the November 3 election. We’re the key to weathering inflation, surviving the next pandemic, and sustaining our freedom. Unlike working people, the rich and their cronies care only about themselves. Related: America’s Dead-End Economy Bad for Everyone For example, CEOs and shareholders oppose legislation to end employer interference in union elections, better safeguard union activists, and impose real penalties on violators. These same moneyed interests resist a bill that would prevent employers from dragging their feet when newly unionized workers come to the table to bargain for the fair contracts they deserve. Corporations even stonewall measures to protect miners from silica exposure and protect healthcare workers from violence on the job. This greed has real consequences. Millions of workers want to join unions but fall short every year because of employer harassment and retaliation. Many have to work multiple bad jobs instead of one good one. Others forgo doctor’s visits because bosses skimp on benefits when there’s no union to hold their feet to the fire. Related: Want to Rebuild the Middle Class? Triple Union Membership Too many of us continue to get sick, sustain injuries, and die because of unsafe working conditions. It would be an understatement to say that we just gave the new Congress a mandate to change all of this. We defied history and beat the odds. We overcame a gerrymandering scheme, voter suppression, billion-dollar misinformation campaigns, intimidation, fearmongering, and other cheating to take a stand. We valued people over money. We won the day. Now it’s time to right the country. Produced by the Independent Media Institute .
